articles.title: Philae Lander Sniffed Out Organics in Comet's Atmosphere
articles.summary: Europe's Philae lander, after its historic landing on Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, made significant scientific discoveries before entering hibernation due to low power. The probe detected organic molecules in the comet's atmosphere and found its surface to be unexpectedly hard, comparable to ice. Despite its short initial operational period, scientists are hopeful for Philae's reactivation as the comet approaches the sun.

articles.title: Jupiter's Red Spot is Likely a Sunburn, Not a Blush
articles.summary: A new analysis of NASA Cassini mission data, combined with laboratory experiments, suggests that Jupiter's Great Red Spot gets its characteristic ruddy color from sunlight breaking down simple chemicals like ammonia and acetylene in the planet's upper atmosphere. Researchers simulated the sun's ultraviolet effects on these gases, producing a reddish material that matched observations of the spot's uppermost cloud layers. This finding contradicts the competing theory that the red color originates from chemicals brought up from deep beneath Jupiter's clouds, instead pointing to a 'sunburn' effect enhanced by the spot's extreme height.

articles.title: SJAA Solar Volunteers at Scouting Encampment at Alameda Fairground
articles.summary: On October 11, 2014, SJAA solar volunteers participated in a large STEM Scouting Encampment at the Alameda County Fairgrounds, focusing on astronomy. They engaged over 500 scouts with solar telescopes, including Lunt Hydrogen-alpha scopes, to observe sunspots, flares, and prominences, while also providing educational talks on the Sun. This successful outreach event, which drew over 1,500 scouts, also featured other scientific exhibits and presentations from NASA and Lawrence Livermore Labs.

articles.title: Solar Sundays
articles.summary: The article reports on past and upcoming "Solar Sunday" observing events, including a recent session at Houge attended by 15 people and an announcement for the next event on December 7th. It also details the return and re-observation of sunspot AR-2192 (renumbered AR-2209) at a Santa Cruz lighthouse viewing session in November, following its superb appearance in October.

articles.title: Fall 2014 SJAA Swap Happiness
articles.summary: The Fall 2014 SJAA Swap Meet was a successful event where members sold and bought used astronomy equipment, making many stargazers happy. The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provided pizza and drinks, collected donations, and received help from numerous volunteers to make the event special.

articles.title: SJAA Member Observation Posts
articles.summary: This article features two detailed observing logs from San Jose Astronomical Association members, Mark McCarthy and Alexander Kramarov, showcasing different observational styles. McCarthy's log empirically details his successful observation of a rare Io-Ganymede transit, complete with precise timings and sketches. Kramarov's more narrative log describes an extensive deep-sky observing session under challenging winter conditions, focusing on Messier objects, constellation identification, and practical preparation for cold-weather astronomy.

articles.title: Kid Spot: Educational Features and Quiz Answers
articles.summary: This "Kid Spot" article offers astronomy-related educational content tailored for a younger audience. It includes space-themed jokes, a quiz with answers, and a 'Night Sky Challenge' for December 2014 detailing visible planets and meteor showers. A significant portion is dedicated to the constellation Pisces, covering its mythology, celestial location, and deep-sky objects like the M74 galaxy.

articles.title: Club Updates
articles.summary: The article provides updates on various resources and programs offered by SJAA, including a new library for members with astronomy books and DVDs. It details the free Telescope Fix It Session where community members can get help with their astronomy gear, and announces regular solar observing sessions held monthly. Additionally, it highlights the Quick STARt Program designed to guide newcomers into amateur astronomy.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board of Directors announced upcoming annual elections in February 2015, with several current members seeking re-election. The article also summarized the November 2014 Board Meeting, highlighting the new quarterly schedule for the Ephemeris newsletter, upcoming Winter Deep Sky Scavenger Hunt dates, and the renewal of the Mendoza Ranch permit. Additionally, it detailed transitions in leadership for the Fix-It and Advanced Loaner Programs and mentioned potential private star parties at Lick Observatory.
